subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient sustains a basilar skull fracture through the ethmoid bone and develops clear rhinorrhea and a complete loss of smell. The fragile nerve fibers that pass through the perforated plate of this bone are sheared by the injury.
question: Which cranial nerve passes through the cribriform plate?
explanation_correct: The olfactory nerve (CN I) passes through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to reach the olfactory bulb in the anterior cranial fossa. Fractures here can shear these fibers, causing anosmia and allowing CSF to leak into the nasal cavity as rhinorrhea.

explanation_incorrect.A: CN II travels through the optic canal together with the ophthalmic artery.
explanation_incorrect.C: CN III exits the middle cranial fossa through the superior orbital fissure.
explanation_incorrect.D: CN VII exits via the internal auditory meatus and subsequently the stylomastoid foramen, not the cribriform plate.
explanation_incorrect.E: CN XII passes through the hypoglossal canal in the occipital bone.

educationalObjective: CN I passes through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone, so basilar fractures here cause anosmia and CSF rhinorrhea.

subject: Neurology
vignette: An orbital tumor compresses several structures as they pass from the middle cranial fossa into the orbit through a slit-like opening in the sphenoid bone. The patient has a dilated pupil, ptosis, inability to abduct the eye, and reduced sensation over the forehead and upper eyelid.
question: Which of the following structures passes through the superior orbital fissure?

options.text: Maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve (V2)
Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3)

explanation_correct: The superior orbital fissure transmits CN III, IV, V1 (ophthalmic division of trigeminal), and VI en route to the orbit. The abducens nerve (CN VI) passes through it to reach the lateral rectus muscle, and the patient's inability to abduct the eye reflects involvement of this nerve at the fissure.

explanation_incorrect.A: V2 exits through the foramen rotundum, not the superior orbital fissure.
explanation_incorrect.B: V3 exits through the foramen ovale together with the accessory meningeal artery.
explanation_incorrect.C: The middle meningeal artery enters the skull through the foramen spinosum.
explanation_incorrect.D: The ophthalmic artery travels through the optic canal accompanied by CN II.

educationalObjective: The superior orbital fissure transmits CN III, IV, V1, and VI.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient with a tumor at the base of the posterior cranial fossa develops hoarseness, dysphagia, weakness of shoulder shrugging, and loss of taste over the posterior third of the tongue. Imaging shows the mass compressing a large venous channel as it exits the skull.
question: Which of the following cranial nerves exits the skull through the jugular foramen?
explanation_correct: The jugular foramen transmits CN IX, X, and XI together with the jugular vein (formed by the sigmoid and inferior petrosal sinuses). A lesion here produces combinations of glossopharyngeal, vagal, and accessory nerve deficits, matching the hoarseness, dysphagia, taste loss, and shoulder weakness in this patient.

explanation_incorrect.B: CN VII exits through the internal auditory meatus with CN VIII and then the stylomastoid foramen, not the jugular foramen.
explanation_incorrect.C: The divisions of CN V exit through the superior orbital fissure (V1), foramen rotundum (V2), and foramen ovale (V3).
explanation_incorrect.D: CN III exits through the superior orbital fissure into the orbit.
explanation_incorrect.E: CN XII passes through the hypoglossal canal in the occipital bone.

educationalObjective: The jugular foramen transmits CN IX, X, and XI along with the jugular vein.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient sustains a temporal bone skull fracture that tears an artery running in a groove along the inner table of the skull, producing an epidural hematoma. The artery enters the middle cranial fossa through a small foramen in the greater wing of the sphenoid bone.
question: Which of the following structures passes through the foramen spinosum?

options.text: Maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve (V2)
Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3)

explanation_correct: The middle meningeal artery, a branch of the maxillary artery, enters the middle cranial fossa through the foramen spinosum and runs in a groove on the inner surface of the temporal and parietal bones. Its laceration in a temporal skull fracture is the classic cause of an epidural hematoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: The ophthalmic artery enters the orbit through the optic canal with CN II.
explanation_incorrect.B: V2 passes through the foramen rotundum, located just medial to the foramen ovale.
explanation_incorrect.D: V3 passes through the foramen ovale, an adjacent but distinct opening from the foramen spinosum.
explanation_incorrect.E: The internal carotid artery enters the cranial cavity through the carotid canal, not the foramen spinosum.

educationalObjective: The foramen spinosum transmits the middle meningeal artery, whose injury causes an epidural hematoma.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A skull-base imaging review identifies four openings: one transmits CN II with the ophthalmic artery; one transmits the mandibular division of CN V; one transmits CN VII and VIII together; and one transmits the vertebral arteries and the spinal root of CN XI. The radiologist must match each foramen to its contents.
question: Which of the following pairings of foramen and structure is correct?

options.text: Optic canal — maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve (V2)
Internal auditory meatus — glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)

explanation_correct: The foramen magnum is the large opening in the occipital bone that transmits the vertebral arteries, the spinal root of CN XI, and the brainstem/spinal cord junction. The other pairings are incorrect because the optic canal carries CN II and the ophthalmic artery, the foramen ovale carries V3, and the internal auditory meatus carries CN VII and VIII.

explanation_incorrect.A: The optic canal transmits CN II and the ophthalmic artery; V2 instead passes through the foramen rotundum.
explanation_incorrect.B: The foramen ovale transmits V3 and the accessory meningeal artery, not the ophthalmic artery.
explanation_incorrect.C: The internal auditory meatus transmits CN VII and VIII; CN IX exits through the jugular foramen.
explanation_incorrect.E: The hypoglossal canal transmits CN XII; CN VII exits via the internal auditory meatus and stylomastoid foramen.

educationalObjective: The foramen magnum transmits the vertebral arteries and the spinal root of CN XI, whereas the optic canal, foramen ovale, and internal auditory meatus have different contents.
